items.title: Mathematical Algorithm Development and Computational Analysis in Support of MDA Flight Test Support
items.context:
The purpose of this Source Sought notice is for market research to identify interested and capability alternative sources for performing mathematical algorithm development and computational analysis in support of Missile Defense Agency (MDA) flight tests. All responses received will be considered for meeting the MDAs requirements and determination of final acquisition strategy for the follow-on contract to HQ085122D0002. This is not a solicitation; request for proposal or quotation. Participation in this effort is voluntary with no cost or obligation to be incurred by the MDA. All costs associated with responding to this Source Sought will be solely at the respondents expense. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this contemplated effort. Submissions of capability statements will be separate from, and have no bearing on, submissions in response to any future Request for Proposal, if one is issued. Eligibility to participate in any future acquisition does not depend upon a response to this notice. The MDA does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice or pay for the information requested. Responses to this notice will be treated as information only and not a proposal. Background: The MDA is responsible for developing and fielding an integrated, layered Missile Defense System (MDS) to protect the United States and its allies from missile attack by providing homeland and regional missile defense. The MDS layered approach includes sensors, kinetic energy systems, directed energy systems, battle management, and command control elements that will engage threats at all ranges and throughout the battlespace. Description: This is a follow-on requirement in support of various programs within the MDA within the Aegis Based Defense (AB) portfolio. The respondents to this request should have the ability to provide equipment and personnel for mathematical algorithm development and analyses for the Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense program, to include current and future capabilities, as identified below. Mathematical Algorithm development and analyses including development and delivery of post intercept debris generation and dynamic behavior models for multi-threaded and massively parallel multi-processor supercomputing systems. Threat Engagement Debris and Kill Assessment Analysis Pre-mission and post mission analysis of flight test event high strain rate, material deformation, projection and trajectory simulations (Velodyne, hydro-structural solver brand name or equal software analysis tool)

items.title: Beach Renourishment, Kennedy Space Center, Brevard County, Florida
items.context:
This announcement constitutes a Source Sought Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking interest from prospective offerors for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 award of the aforementioned project. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gauge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of the Construction and Dredging Communities, to include Small Businesses, as the Government must ensure there is adequate competition amongst the potential pool of responsible contractors. The notice is also soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for this large-scale construction project exceeding $35,000,000. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said notice or any follow-up information requested. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of an Invitation For Bid (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said sources sought notice or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The proposed project work will consist of nourishing approximately 4.1 miles shoreline along Kennedy Space Center between FDEP Range Monuments V-366 and V-386 in Brevard County, Florida. The project includes dredging approximately 2.5 million cubic yards (MCY) of material for construction of a beach berm and dune. Beach compatible sand for the project may be dredged from up to three (3) offshore borrow areas. Chester Shoals I is located east of Cape Canaveral in State waters and is centered approximately 1.7 miles offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Kennedy Shoals and Hetzel Shoals are located east of Cape Canaveral in Federal waters and are centered approximately 4.5 miles and 10 miles, respectively, offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Project work also includes, but is not limited to, beach tilling, turbidity monitoring, environmental species monitoring, and Munitions and Explosive of Concern (MEC) support. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 280 calendar days after issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP), including 60 calendar days to commence work. items.title: Kissimmee River Restoration (KRR) Project, S-69 Weir Repair
items.context:
BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The South Atlantic Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (SAJ) is seeking interest from prospective bidders for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 contract award for the subject construction project. SAJ has a requirement for the repair of components of the existing S-69 weir structure inclusive of sheet piles concrete cap and ancillary concrete driving slab. The purpose of this sources sought is to gauge interest, capabilities, and qualifications of contractors that have experience in completing similar projects. The scope of the contract is inclusive of but not limited to (a) partial concrete cap demolition, (b) inspection and cleaning of existing concrete, steel bars, anchor studs and steel sheet piles, (c) preparation of studs and rebar, (d) installation of new closed-loop epoxy coated stirrups routed through the sheet pile and new anchor studs welded to the sheet pile, (e) provision of new expansion joints, (f) repairing of concrete caps with structural concrete, (g) driving slab subsurface void investigation and subsequent repairs to address separation of the slab from sheet pile, and (h) all quality control and construction administration submittals relevant to the construction effort, including as-builts of the final repaired structure. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of a Request for Proposal (RFP). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The S-69 Weir consists of driven sheet pile walls with a concrete cap that acts as a weir and is a key feature of the Kissimmee River Restoration (KRR) Project. Located in Okeechobee and Highlands Counties, Florida, the weirs primary function is to restore the Kissimmee Rivers floodplain hydrology to pre-canal conditions by controlling water stages and discharges into the C-38 canal. Repair of components of the existing S-69 weir structure require sheet pile concrete cap and driving concrete slab. Anticipated work includes but is not limited to: concrete removal portions of the cap, addition of new reinforcement steel closed stirrups, welding of anchor studs, providing expansion joint material, casting-in-place new structural concrete, assessment of voids underneath the driving slab through concrete coring and grouting of cored holes, and filling of gaps between the slab and cap with Controlled Low Strength Material (CSLM) or equivalent approved flowable fill. The overall project site components encompass work to done at the following approximate location: 27.334767, -81.032830; very close to the Chandler Slough South Trailhead. items.title: Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness and Validation Status
items.context: Relevant policy, standards, and guidance include, but may not be limited to: NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program; FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules; FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard; FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard; FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard; NIST SP 800-208, Recommendation for Stateful Hash-Based Signature Schemes; NIST SP 800-52, Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of Transport Layer Security Implementations; OMB Memorandum M-22-09, Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles; Executive Order 14306, Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nations Cybersecurity; Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks; OMB Memorandum M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography; and CISA guidance regarding product categories and technologies that use post-quantum cryptography standards. This RFI is intended to collect industry information regarding the availability, validation status, product and service readiness, procurement accessibility, implementation maturity, operational impacts, interoperability, and migration support associated with commercial products and services that support, or plan to support, NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography standards. This Request for Information is issued for market research purposes only. There are no anticipated tasks under this RFI. This RFI is intended to collect information from industry regarding vendor capabilities, products and services availability, cryptographic validation status, contract accessibility, and readiness to support the Federal Governments migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or promise to issue a future solicitation. Any contract or order that may result from information received through this RFI will be subject to applicable procurement laws, regulations, and competition requirements. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred by industry in preparing or submitting responses to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the respondents expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation, if one is issued. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.
